C0.quote: We study the computational complexity of finding the possible and necessary winners
C0.note: Computational aspects of voting rules (possible/necessary winners) under incomplete information.

C1.quote: Complexity results for computing the necessary and possible winners
C1.note: All results are algorithms or NP-completeness.

C2.1.value: ranking profile; approval profile; partial spatial profile
C2.1.quote: A ranking profile R = (R1 , . . . , Rn ) consists of n linear orders

C2.2.quote: Ai denotes the set of candidates that the voter vi “approves.”
C2.2.note: Rankings derived from spatial positions; approval for k-approval and AV.

C2.3.quote: Each Ri represents the preference order of voter vi .
C2.3.note: Ideal points and preferences are held attitudes; ranking derived from ideal points.

C2.4.quote: each voter vj ranks candidates in C according to their Euclidean distance
C2.4.note: Rankings are constructed from ideal points and the rule applied directly; no statement on submission or reporting.

C3.1.note: No analysis considers misreporting; the conclusion only mentions candidate strategic considerations as future work.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.note: No voter utility, welfare, or cost notions are used.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.note: Only possible/necessary winner complexity is studied.

VOT.note: Voters have uncertain ideal points but take no action in the model.

CAN.note: Candidates are fixed alternatives; relocation is mentioned only as future work.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

C9.1.note: Abstract, introduction and conclusion summarise technical results; no claims on real institutions, voter well-being, or which rule to use.
